# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 43

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Disagreement 1 — 43:2 "takes the first seat" vs. "desires the seat of honor" vs. "always wants the best seat"

- **EMET:** "wishes to take the first seat"
- **LOGOS:** "desires the seat of honor"
- **PNEUMA:** "always wants the best seat"
- **Greek:** *thelei protōkathédrian echein* — wishes to have the seat of first/prominence
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "seeks the seat of honor" (LOGOS adjusted). *Prōtokathédria* is the honored first seat; "seat of honor" captures both "first" and the honor context.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 43:2 "bold and shameless and talkative" vs. "bold and shameless and loquacious"

- **EMET:** "bold and shameless and talkative"
- **LOGOS:** "bold and shameless and loquacious"
- **PNEUMA:** "bold, shameless, and a nonstop talker"
- **Greek:** *tolmēros kai anaides kai polylalos* — bold/daring, shameless/impudent, much-speaking
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "bold and shameless and loquacious" (LOGOS). *Polylalos* = much-speaking/loquacious; "loquacious" is more precise than "talkative" (EMET) or the colloquial PNEUMA rendering.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 43:2 "takes payment for his prophesying"

- **EMET:** "takes payment for his prophesying"
- **LOGOS:** "accepts payment for his prophesying"
- **PNEUMA:** "charges money for his prophecies"
- **Greek:** *misthoù propheteuei* — prophesies for wages/pay
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "accepts payment for his prophesying" (LOGOS). "Accepts" implies receipt of something offered; "charges" (PNEUMA) implies active solicitation. The text says he takes whatever is offered.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 43:3 "empty desire" vs. "vain desire"

- **EMET:** "vain desire of this world"
- **LOGOS:** "empty desire of this age"
- **PNEUMA:** "worldly craving"
- **Greek:** *epithumia tou aiōnos toutou* — desire of this age
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "empty desire of this age" (LOGOS). *Aiōn* = age, not "world" (*kosmos*); EMET's "world" mistranslates the term; "craving" (PNEUMA) adds intensity not in the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 43:3 "makes himself more lowly than all men"

- **EMET:** "makes himself more lowly than all men"
- **LOGOS:** "makes himself more lowly than all men"
- **PNEUMA:** "considers himself lower than everyone else"
- **Greek:** *tapeinoteron pantōn anthrōpōn heauton poiei* — makes himself more lowly/humble than all people
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "makes himself more lowly than all men." EMET and LOGOS agree; PNEUMA's "considers himself" loses the active self-lowering.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 43:3 "answers no one when asked" vs. "does not respond when questioned"

- **EMET:** "answers no one when asked"
- **LOGOS:** "does not respond when asked a question"
- **PNEUMA:** "doesn't jump in to answer questions on his own initiative"
- **Greek:** *oudeni apokrinetal erōtōmenos* — does not answer anyone when questioned
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "does not respond when questioned" (LOGOS). PNEUMA adds "on his own initiative" which partially misrepresents the point — the true prophet does answer eventually, but only when the Spirit moves him.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 43:4 "Such is the power of the Spirit of the Lord"

- **EMET:** "Such therefore is the power of the Lord's Spirit"
- **LOGOS:** "Such is the power of the Spirit of the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "That is the nature of the Lord's Spirit"
- **Greek:** *hē dynamis tou pneumatos tou kyriou* — the power of the Spirit of the Lord
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "Such is the power of the Spirit of the Lord" (LOGOS). "Nature" (PNEUMA) loses the *dynamis* (power) concept which is important — Hermas uses power language precisely.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 43:5 repetition of false prophet description

- **EMET:** Preserves the repetition of 43:2 almost verbatim
- **LOGOS:** Preserves the repetition with minor variation ("deceits" vs. "deceptions")
- **PNEUMA:** Substantially paraphrases the repetition
- **Note:** Hermas deliberately repeats the vice list; this is a rhetorical device
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA preserves the repetition, following EMET/LOGOS. The repetition functions as a drum-beat emphasis and should not be collapsed.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 43:6 "does not inquire...by means of money" vs. "does not seek payment"

- **EMET:** "neither does he inquire about anything by means of money"
- **LOGOS:** "nor does he make inquiry for money"
- **PNEUMA:** "doesn't live lavishly or seek money for answering questions"
- **Greek:** *ou zētei... dia chrēmatōn* — does not seek/ask... through money
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "nor does he seek payment for inquiry" (blending LOGOS/EMET). The contrast with the false prophet who accepts payment is the key point.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 43:6 "answers not by himself, but rather by the will of God"

- **EMET:** "he answers not by himself, but rather by the will of God"
- **LOGOS:** "he does not answer of himself but only by the will of God"
- **PNEUMA:** "he doesn't answer on his own — only on the basis of God's will"
- **Greek:** *aph' heautou ou legalei alla kata to thelēma tou theou* — does not speak from himself but according to the will of God
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he does not answer of himself but only by the will of God" (LOGOS). "Of himself" preserves the Greek reflexive pronoun idiom.

---

## Disagreement 11 — 43:7 "upright life" vs. "upright and virtuous manner of living"

- **EMET:** "consistent with upright life"
- **LOGOS:** "consistent with an upright and virtuous manner of living"
- **PNEUMA:** "line up with righteous, godly conduct"
- **Greek:** *kata tēn zōēn orthotomei* — walks straight/consistent with the life
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "consistent with upright living" (EMET simplified). LOGOS adds "virtuous" beyond the Greek; PNEUMA's "godly" adds theological coloring not present.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 43.*
